blocks.explanation:
A single function whose antiderivative we do not know directly.
Plan: write \(\ln x = \ln x \cdot 1\), take \(\ln x\) as the first function and 1 as the second, and integrate by parts.
steps:
Given: \(\int \ln x\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: integration by parts with \(f(x) = \ln x\) (easy to differentiate) and \(g(x) = 1\) (easy to integrate).

Write as a product
\[\int \ln x\,dx = \int \ln x\cdot 1\,dx\]
Why: the formula needs two functions; multiplying by 1 changes nothing.

Apply integration by parts
\[= \ln x\cdot x - \int x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[= x\ln x - \int 1\,dx\]
Why: \(\int 1\,dx = x\) and \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln x = \frac{1}{x}\); then \(x\cdot\frac{1}{x} = 1\).

Integrate
\[= x\ln x - x + c\]
Why: \(\int 1\,dx = x\); one constant at the end.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\ln x - x) = \ln x + x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} - 1\]
\[= \ln x\]
Why: product rule on \(x\ln x\); we get back the integrand.
